verified_uncited_book_records.field: 小 headword; PDF p. 76, printed p. 64; continuation PDF p. 77, printed p. 65
verified_uncited_book_records.text: The inspected entry calls 小 pictographic, interpreting its marks as tiny dust or sand particles and describing 小 as an early graph of 沙. It says the graph extended to mean ‘small,’ opposite 大, and reports that sense in oracle-bone and bronze inscriptions, citing 《粹》1004 for 小雨. It describes later extensions to low status, contempt and youth. It says the graph had become corrupted in bronze inscriptions and treats Shuowen’s 八-plus-丨 account as an explanation of that altered form. The adjacent 少 entry says 小 and 少 were originally one graph, used similarly in oracle-bone texts, and later differentiated; its account continues on printed p. 65. Both attached page images were inspected. Forms checked against scan pixels: 小, 少, 沙, 八, 丨, 大, and 《粹》1004. This verifies what this author claims, not the disputed sand-grain interpretation.
